# R115 generator terms review (Groq-hosted `openai/gpt-oss-120b`)

**Status:** review record, 2026-10-24 (sources accessed that day). **Not legal advice**; the
unresolved item below needs a team / legal decision. Protocol v5 is unchanged by this review.

## Scope

Protocol v5 uses the R115 dataset (`Ridham115/indian-scam-sms-synthetic-audited`, revision
`45e92c38ba20e973ef3ff5d1893a0a710f622018`, file SHA-256 `45bde5f1…61e2`, CC BY 4.0) as a
**training-only** source, restricted by `sources.R115.generators_used` to rows generated by
`groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b`.

- The dataset card lists 700 gpt-oss-120b rows and 880 Gemini rows (861 + 19). The v5 dry run
  loads exactly 700 R115 rows (357 scam, 343 safe) and records 880 `excluded_generator` rows, so
  **no Gemini output is used** (the card warns that Gemini terms may bar using Gemini outputs to
  develop competing models).
- After deduplication and the G4 purge, 696 R115 rows remain in the v5 pool. R115 never enters
  the frozen test (it is not test-eligible).

## Verified sources

| Source | What it says (relevant parts) |
|---|---|
| R115 dataset card, huggingface.co/datasets/Ridham115/indian-scam-sms-synthetic-audited | Released under **CC BY 4.0**. "Those providers' terms apply to their outputs and may restrict some uses … CC BY 4.0 does not override those terms; you are responsible for checking them for your use." Generators: gemini-3.5-flash-lite 861, gemini-3.7-flash 19, groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b 700. |
| gpt-oss-120b model card, huggingface.co/openai/gpt-oss-120b | Model licence **Apache 2.0**. No restriction on using outputs (including for training other models) is stated. |
| gpt-oss `USAGE_POLICY` (same repository) | Aims for safe, responsible, democratic use; users must comply with applicable law. No restriction on using outputs to build datasets or train models. Applies to users *of the model*. |
| Groq Services Agreement, console.groq.com/docs/legal/services-agreement (last modified 2026-06-22) | §8.1 the Customer "retains all Intellectual Property Rights in Customer Data (including in Inputs and Outputs)"; §1 "Outputs are Customer Data"; §4.1 Customer complies with the applicable AI Model Terms (here: Apache 2.0 + gpt-oss usage policy); §4.2 Groq may not train on Inputs/Outputs, and the Customer is "solely responsible for all use of the Outputs"; §4.3 use discretion before publishing Output; §6.3(e) no use of the Cloud Services to build competing services; no clause found that passes restrictions on Outputs to downstream recipients. |
| Groq Acceptable Use & Responsible AI Policy, console.groq.com/docs/legal/ai-policy (effective 2025-10-15; ranks above the Agreement) | Applies to a Customer's use of Groq Cloud/AI Model Services. Prohibits use "for any … fraudulent purpose", "for any misrepresentation, misinformation, disinformation, or any misleading or deceptive activities", "for phishing, generating, or distributing malware", and unsolicited mass solicitations. Customers with adequate safeguards needing flexibility "for lawful business or research purposes, may contact Groq to request an exception". No explicit provision for generating harmful examples for detection or classifier training. |
| Groq Service Specific Terms (effective 2025-11-13) and Terms of Use (effective 2025-10-15) | No Output-use terms relevant here; gpt-oss is not named; the Terms of Use do not apply to cloud services. |

## Assessment

1. **SatyaLens's position.** SatyaLens did not call Groq or run gpt-oss to create R115; it uses a
   published dataset. The Groq Agreement and AUP bind the *dataset author* (the Groq Customer),
   not downstream dataset users. Under §8.1 the author holds the IP in the Outputs, so the
   author could license them under CC BY 4.0. **No verified term restricts SatyaLens's use of
   the gpt-oss rows for training a scam-detection classifier**, provided CC BY 4.0 attribution
   is kept (protocol v5 `sources.R115.title` and the pool provenance record it).
2. **gpt-oss terms.** Apache 2.0 and the usage policy govern use *of the model*; they place no
   restriction on its outputs. Nothing indicates they restrict SatyaLens.

## Unresolved (do not assume permission)

- **U1: Groq AUP compliance at generation time.** R115 consists of synthetic scam, phishing-style
  SMS. The AUP prohibits fraudulent, deceptive and phishing uses, and offers research exceptions
  only on request. The dataset card does not say whether the author requested or held an
  exception. Generating labelled examples for detection research may or may not count as a
  prohibited "phishing"/"deceptive" use; the AUP does not address it. This concerns the
  **author's** conduct and the dataset's provenance, not a licence term binding SatyaLens. It is
  still an **open provenance and ethics question**.
- **U2: Terms version.** The Groq Agreement and AUP reviewed are the current versions. The
  versions in force when R115 was generated, and any offline agreement the author may have
  signed, could not be verified. The dataset card shows no generation date.
- **U3: Third-party summaries.** ConductAtlas pages were seen in search results but **not relied
  on**; only Groq's, OpenAI's and Hugging Face's own pages were used.

## Decision (2026-10-24)

The project owner chose **Option A**: R115 (gpt-oss-120b rows only) is retained under protocol v5
unchanged. U1 (generator provenance under the Groq AUP) and U2 (historical terms versions) remain
**open residual risks**. Permission for the generation of R115 was **not independently verified**;
the only verified grant to SatyaLens is the dataset's CC BY 4.0 licence. Revisit this record if
the dataset author or Groq provides information, or before any public release of a model trained
on R115.

## Options considered

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| A. Proceed under protocol v5 as written | CC BY 4.0 licence; U1/U2 stay documented residual risks. |
| B. Ask the dataset author whether a Groq research exception or equivalent permission was obtained, before sealing | Resolves U1/U2 if answered; may delay sealing. |
| C. Exclude R115 entirely | Requires a new protocol version (v6). R115 is training-only and ranks below every test-eligible source (DONATION, IMC25, MWOZ_TEST) in dedup priority, so the frozen test's membership would not change, but the pool, its SHA-256 and `pool_counts` would (and SYN rows R115 currently displaces could return). After sealing under v5 this would mean a reseal under a new protocol. |
